meta.title: How Bangalore became India's tech capital

scenes.narration: In 1985, Bangalore was a quiet city of gardens.
People called it a pensioners' paradise.

scenes.note: 1985 — Miller's Road, Bangalore. Texas Instruments opens India's first multinational R&D centre.
scenes.narration: Then an American chip company did something nobody expected.
Its satellite dish, the link to the world, arrived on a ==bullock cart.==
Forty years later, the engineers took over.
Glass tech parks rose where the fields used to be.

scenes.label: tech workers in ==one city==
scenes.narration: Today, more than a million tech workers live in this one city.
Its state now produces forty one percent of India's software exports.
From a bullock cart, to the city that codes the world.
